answer: An opal records a fracture, so every claim must show where it broke. Each identity needs two holders outside its own haven to countersign its opal, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n separate witnesses instead of a single ring. Every opal is priced by rank: the k-th claim an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A comet audit replays a random fracture each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim clears the haven and forfeits its bonds, which cannot be pooled or resold.
